findings.title: Data race on shared err variable across concurrent index builds in init()
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, each errgroup goroutine does `_, _, err = s.build(ctx, ...)` writing to the same `err` variable captured from the outer function scope, then `return err`. With this PR the bleve backend's BuildIndex no longer holds a global lock for the whole build, so these goroutines genuinely run in parallel for the first time. Concurrent writes to `err` are a data race (flagged by the race detector), and worse, a failing goroutine can have its error overwritten by another goroutine's nil before it executes `return err` — so group.Wait() can return nil even though an index failed to build, letting startup proceed with a silently missing index. Each goroutine should use a local variable: `_, _, err := s.build(...); return err`.

findings.title: Unsynchronized totalBatchesIndexed++ inside parallel goroutines
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, `totalBatchesIndexed++` is executed inside errgroup goroutines that now run concurrently (previously their work was effectively serialized by the bleve backend's global BuildIndex lock). This is a data race and the count reported in the span event 'namespaces indexed' will be wrong under concurrency. Use an atomic counter or aggregate after Wait().

findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex for the same key can corrupt file-based indexes and leak index objects
findings.body: Removing the global cacheMu lock from BuildIndex means two goroutines can now build the same NamespacedResource simultaneously: getOrCreateIndex in search.go does GetIndex-then-build with no per-key synchronization (its own TODO acknowledges this), and it is reachable concurrently from Search and handleEvent. For indexes above FileThreshold both builds call bleve.New on the same directory concurrently, which can fail or corrupt the on-disk index; for memory indexes the work is duplicated and the second `b.cache[key] = idx` silently overwrites the first, orphaning an open bleve.Index that is never closed and double-counting the IndexTenants metric. BuildIndex should take a per-key lock (or re-check the cache under the write lock and return the existing index) now that the coarse lock is gone.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no lock while BuildIndex now writes b.cache[key] under cacheMu (GetIndex uses RLock). This is an unsynchronized concurrent map read/write that can panic with 'fatal error: concurrent map read and map write'. The window is real: search.init starts the watch-events goroutine (whose handleEvent can trigger on-demand builds via getOrCreateIndex for namespaces/kinds skipped at startup) immediately before calling s.search.TotalDocs() in the 'search index initialized' log line. Take cacheMu.RLock() around the iteration in TotalDocs.

findings.title: NewResourceServer error path leaks started goroutines and the cancel func
findings.body: Now that s.Init(ctx) runs eagerly in NewResourceServer, a failure partway through init (e.g. search.init succeeded and started its watch goroutine, then initWatcher failed, or any init error) returns nil, err without calling s.cancel(). The server's internal cancellable context is never cancelled and any background goroutines already started keep running with nothing able to stop them (the search watch goroutine runs on context.Background(), independent of s.ctx). On init failure the constructor should call s.cancel() / Stop() to unwind what was started before returning the error.
